entries.content_plain:
Introduction

 David consults with his officers, and resolves to bring back the ark from the house of Abinadab, 1Chr 13:1-4 . They place it on a new cart, and Uzza and Ahio drive the cart; the oxen stumbling, Uzza puts forth his hand to save the ark from falling, and he is smitten by the Lord, 1Chr 13:5-10 . David is displeased, and orders the ark to be carried to the house of Obed-edom the Gittite, 1Chr 13:11-13 . The ark abides there three months, and the Lord blesses Obed-edom, 1Chr 13:14 .

entries.content_osis: <hi type="bold">Verse 14</hi> <div eID="gen13612" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen13613" type="x-p"/> The Lord blessed the house of Obed-edom - That this man was only a sojourner at Gath, whence he was termed Gittite, and that he was originally a Levite, is evident from <reference osisRef="1Chr.15.17">1Chr 15:17</reference>, <reference osisRef="1Chr.15.18">1Chr 15:18</reference>. <div eID="gen13613" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen13614" type="x-p"/> The Targum ends this chapter thus: "And the Word of the Lord blessed Obed-edom, and his children, and his grand-children; and his wife conceived, and his eight daughters-in-law: and each brought forth eight at one birth, insomuch that in one day there were found, of fathers and children, fourscore and one; and He blessed and increased greatly all that belonged to him." This exposition will not be generally received; but all rabbins must be allowed to deal in the marvellous. <div eID="gen13614" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen13615" type="x-p"/> For other remarks see on <reference osisRef="2Sam.6.1">2Sam 6:1</reference> (note), etc.  <chapter eID="1Chr.13"/> <div eID="gen13615" type="x-p"/>
entries.content_plain:
Verse 14 

 The Lord blessed the house of Obed-edom - That this man was only a sojourner at Gath, whence he was termed Gittite, and that he was originally a Levite, is evident from 1Chr 15:17 , 1Chr 15:18 . 

 The Targum ends this chapter thus: "And the Word of the Lord blessed Obed-edom, and his children, and his grand-children; and his wife conceived, and his eight daughters-in-law: and each brought forth eight at one birth, insomuch that in one day there were found, of fathers and children, fourscore and one; and He blessed and increased greatly all that belonged to him." This exposition will not be generally received; but all rabbins must be allowed to deal in the marvellous. 

 For other remarks see on 2Sam 6:1 (note), etc.
